issues.on_page: Total Governmental Funds column by object; Street Fund share e.g. Salaries 11,172.13, Insurance 7,946.28, Repair and Maintenance 5,410.49, Utilities 7,243.38 (pp6-7)
issues.issue: The governmental statement lists spending only by object. Every Total-column object line except Library is recorded as general government, although much of it is Street Fund spending (the per-fund detail correctly uses streets/highways). This follows the Total-column rule, so it is a judgment call.

The user's capital outlay rule requires the label 'Capital Outlay: <function>'. The fund is the General Fund, so 'Capital Outlay: General Government' with computed would fit. The statement line disbursements[16] (44,040.76, General plus Street) keeps 'Capital outlay' because no single function is printed, which is defensible.

issues.on_page: Sales Tax 16,832.52 (Light Fund operating receipts); Statement of Activities p4 lists it under Charges for Services against Sales Tax Remittance 18,289.10
issues.issue: This is sales tax collected on electric sales and passed through to the state, not the village's own sales-tax revenue. The printed label supports the category, but the report counts the amount in Charges for Services. The same applies to detail[60].
Customer meter deposits are not clearly a charge for services. The category was carried over from FY2024 with no evidence on the page. The same applies to detail[11]. It is already marked review.

The extractor rules say Homestead Exemption and Property Tax Credit are each also used as their own detail_category. detail[5] and [18] (Homestead Exemption) and detail[6] and [19] (Property Tax Credit) use the generic name instead. The name is on the list, so this is an inconsistency, not an error.
Sales tax paid to the state is neither a tax refund nor a treasurer fee. The category Other Taxes Paid is right. This is a judgment call on the detail name.
The category is Interest Income but the detail_category is 'investment income'. The same applies to detail[25] and [75]. Other reports use 'Interest Income' for both fields on plain interest lines.
None of the equity lines has a category, while other reports categorize equity lines. The amounts are correct.
